submissions.message:
LeRoy! I have such good memories of playing pickleball together and installing Aunt Karen’s storm door in the dark. You have been so kind to me and I am praying for your health right now and praying for your relationship with Jesus. We never talked explicitly about that, so I don’t know exactly where you are, but Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6) and He is merciful and gracious and will forgive all our sins and call us His own. He is making all things right and will one day remove all pain and dry all our tears. He is renewing all creation and hates wickedness so much that He is removing is from the cosmos and died to make that happen. “because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.(Romans 10:9, ESV)
For "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." (Romans 10:13, ESV)

Thank you for caring for my Aunt Karen and being a good friend to her. I hope to see you on the pickleball court sometime soon!

submissions.name: Millie Wibert
submissions.message:
I feel very fortunate that growing up, our family was close with the Brandon-Harvey family.

One beautiful Michigan summer, our families rented a cabin together near Traverse City. One day, we all made the trip to Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore.

I remember we had all made the long trek, including the famous steep climb down the dune, when someone realized something important had been left back in the car. I honestly can’t remember what the missing item was. What I do remember, clear as day, was Leroy and his selfless act. Without missing a beat, he volunteered to make the climb back up the dune, all the way to the car, and then back again to all of us. A journey that felt daunting enough to do once, he was happy to take on twice for the rest of us. That memory has always stuck with me and captures Leroy perfectly. Kind, always willing to go the extra mile for others (quite literally), and with enough stamina to make the rest of us question our life choices.

I also can’t leave out Leroy helping Molly and me produce our hit song, Swim, and even playing guitar on it. Not many adults are willing to spend that kind of quality time with kids, let alone help them bring their big creative ideas to life. At the time, it felt like the coolest thing ever… and honestly, it still does.

I’m so lucky to have Leroy Harvey in my life. As I’ve gotten to raise my own daughter, it’s really put into perspective just how important it is to have loving, wonderful people in your life beyond your parents. Leroy has made a profound impact on my life, and I can only hope my baby girl Madeline has that same love and luck in her life that I’ve been so fortunate to have.

And since Leroy wanted to hear about the good things happening in our lives, I had to share this picture of my sweet daughter, Madeline. Becoming her mom has brought more joy to my life than I ever could have imagined.

Several months ago, I was pumping gas when I looked over and saw her smiling at me from her car seat. I remember having this sudden realization that she somehow makes even the most ordinary, everyday chores feel special. I quickly snapped this picture because I never wanted to forget that moment.

One of my very favorite parts of being her mom is getting to watch her experience the first joys of life. It’s like every experience becomes new again through her eyes, and I get to experience it all over again right alongside her for the very first time.

Love you, Leroy!

Dear Leroy,
I have known you for a couple of decades. Although we have had very little direct communication over the years, the thought of you and the sight of you have made me smile consistently all these years.

The first time I noticed you was at the Fellowship when I happened to notice you and your young son, arms around one another, singing together from the hymnal. My thought was, “Who is that father? What a gift he is giving to his son by bringing him into this loving community and making music with him.”

After that, I always noticed you at the Fellowship and smiled at the sight of you.

Several years later, with little or no direct conversation, you blew my mind. Maybe you remember the event. I was working with the Michigan Department of Community Health on the “Walkable Communities” initiative. We had a representative of the CDC coming to see how Michigan was spending the grant money we’d been given by CDC, some of which had gone to the Allen Street Center. I drove him to a meeting you were having with all your sub grantees, at which you asked each person present to tell what their little bit of grant money. 

Maybe you remember what I told you about the CDC guy’s reaction to what he had heard from your grantees. He said, with a huge amount of enthusiasm, “Well, I am glad that my tax dollars are being used for these projects.“ I was glad that you had made us look good, but I was thrilled to see the creative used to which you had put the small amounts of money. They were all doing things that could really make a difference.

I’m not sure at what point I learned who your mother was. I could see where your concern for the environment came from. Knowing that she could sometimes be a bit challenging to be around, I was dazzled by your kindness and loving attitude toward her. I wasn’t present at the Fellowship when you gave a Mother’s Day tribute to her, but I heard about it. Wow.

The next time I noticed you was in the context of recycling. I’m not sure all the different roles you have played, but I felt my community was truly blessed by having you in a stewardship role for our environment. I’m sure none of those jobs paid a lot of money, I assumed that taking care of the environment was more of a vocation for you than a job.

The other context in which you made me smile was your musicianship. I saw you making music at the Fellowship and in a few other informal venues. Your choice of music and the sound you put out never failed to warm my heart and bring me joy.

I am sorry that my life path did not intersect more with yours. Truly, I have seen you as a Point of Light in the world. What you leave behind will not disappear when you are gone. 

With love,
Karen Petersmarck
May 13, 2026

Dear Leroy,    Hey my dear friend.  This is the first I've heard ANYTHING about your health journey.  It sounds like you are into a pretty intense time of it, it being life.  I don't even remember the last time we talked!  Are you having guests?  Anyway.  Let me share about my own health journey recently, like the last three years, about.  After a squabble with my little sister over our parent's Crosley Family Living Trust, I feel into serious depression about Jan. 2023 and ended up in McLaren GEMS  (Geriatric Evaluation and Management Services) unit for the month of March, 2023.  No fun at all and I was happy to get out.  It's been a struggle to keep going at times, ever since.  My practice of bhakti-yoga (Krsna consciousness) and pranayam and some helpful medication has helped me feel more energetic the past few months. I feel very grateful for the distinct lack of suffering I've been experiencing some over the last few months and I'm hoping to keep the trend going!  I turned 76 in January and boy if that isn't a trip.  My humorist Dad told me that old age isn't for sisies :>) He was right.
Anyway.  My son Prema will be 45 in July and him and sweet Vanessa have my two granddaughters Sophia, 10 and Ella, 8.  I am very happy for them.  Prema has his own company called BCS Tile Solutions with two of his buddies. They have about 20 employees and they work the Minneapolis metro area with some blessed success.  I do ask Prema once in a while how much of his wealth is he going to take with him when he leaves his body!! We chuckle at that.  However, self-realization does remain my own first priority.  I feel so fortunate to be a bhakti-yogi or at least trying sincerely to be.  I think about the old Urban Option days sometimes, very fondly........Oil paint :>) :>(   Again, LeRoy you have all my prayers and if you are entertaining any guests, I would be greatly honored to share some quality time with you.  w/ love, Eric Crosley / aka / Antariksa das

LeRoy -

Sorry to hear that you are having health issues. I have had two of my four brothers die in a little over a year. My older brother, Frank, after a long bout with bone cancer but staying mostly in his own home with visits from hospice and from the VA. He had served as a Marine in Vietnam where he was exposed to Agent Orange, so he had that support as well as many visits from his 2 daughters and his four brothers. He was often in pain during the last six years or so of his life, but even so, he had one of the best days the month before he passed on participating form his front porch in his small town parade that he had usually helped to organize. And he continued to the end to participate in our family get-together early each summer.

Then, just ofter returning home from Frank's memorial service my next younger brother Roy, who was a forester and alwaya signed his emails "may the forest be with you!" passed on suddenly and unexpectedly of a heart attack. At Roy's service my brothers and I were overwhelmed by both the number of people who showed up at pavilion near the top of a mountain to walk a trail in his honor, then stayed on to tell both heartwarming  and amusing stories about Roy and his unique approach to life. Many of the stories were about seeing him out fishing in nothing but his "Tighty-Whities". Or about his approach to games. He would add or blacken squares in crossword puzzles to accommodate his answers and in word games he played with the family he would make up words.

So now I am the oldest of only 3 remaining brothers. I think you know my ex-wife, and best friend, Nancy Rygwelski. She has recently been diagnosed with stage 3 melanoma. I forwarded the email I am replying to now to Nancy, so you will likely hear from her if she is not feeling too bad. I feel very fortunate that growing up, our family was close with the Brandon-Harvey family.

One beautiful Michigan summer, our families rented a cabin together near Traverse City. One day, we all made the trip to Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore.

I remember we had all made the long trek, including the famous steep climb down the dune, when someone realized something important had been left back in the car. I honestly can’t remember what the missing item was. What I do remember, clear as day, was Leroy and his selfless act. Without missing a beat, he volunteered to make the climb back up the dune, all the way to the car, and then back again to all of us. A journey that felt daunting enough to do once, he was happy to take on twice for the rest of us. That memory has always stuck with me and captures Leroy perfectly. Kind, always willing to go the extra mile for others (quite literally), and with enough stamina to make the rest of us question our life choices.

I also can’t leave out Leroy helping Molly and me produce our hit song, Swim, and even playing guitar on it. Not many adults are willing to spend that kind of quality time with kids, let alone help them bring their big creative ideas to life. At the time, it felt like the coolest thing ever… and honestly, it still does.

I’m so lucky to have Leroy Harvey in my life. As I’ve gotten to raise my own daughter, it’s really put into perspective just how important it is to have loving, wonderful people in your life beyond your parents. Leroy has made a profound impact on my life, and I can only hope my baby girl Madeline has that same love and luck in her life that I’ve been so fortunate to have.

And since Leroy wanted to hear about the good things happening in our lives, I had to share this picture of my sweet daughter, Madeline. Becoming her mom has brought more joy to my life than I ever could have imagined.

Several months ago, I was pumping gas when I looked over and saw her smiling at me from her car seat. I remember having this sudden realization that she somehow makes even the most ordinary, everyday chores feel special. I quickly snapped this picture because I never wanted to forget that moment.

One of my very favorite parts of being her mom is getting to watch her experience the first joys of life. It’s like every experience becomes new again through her eyes, and I get to experience it all over again right alongside her for the very first time.

Love you, Leroy!
Helllo
